question: Should memory-wiki isolation be solved through a generic agents.list[].plugins override contract, a memory-wiki-specific per-agent vault contract, or documented unsupported shared-gateway isolation?
rationale: The request changes config/API and security boundaries for durable memory state, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent contract or compatibility behavior from source evidence alone.

options.title: Design generic agent-scoped plugin config
options.body: Add a shared plugin config override contract with explicit precedence, validation, SecretRef handling, lifecycle/restart semantics, doctor behavior, and memory-wiki coverage.

options.title: Add memory-wiki-specific vault routing
options.body: Keep plugin config global and add a narrower memory-wiki per-agent vault map or mode, reducing generic API surface but leaving related plugin config needs to separate issues.

options.title: Document separate gateways as the isolation boundary
options.body: Close the feature path for now and document that memory-wiki is shared per gateway unless operators isolate agents by process or install, avoiding new config surface at the cost of user friction.

recommendation.title: Design generic agent-scoped plugin config
recommendation.body: Add a shared plugin config override contract with explicit precedence, validation, SecretRef handling, lifecycle/restart semantics, doctor behavior, and memory-wiki coverage.
